claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, the stage lock only protects an execution once it is actually running: a newer execution can still overtake an execution that is waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it ever starts.

If a CodePipeline CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up` and enough commits land while it's busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.

Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn, rather than a later commit replacing an earlier one that never got its turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the CodePipeline pipeline.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can be used to set the pipeline `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider has `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is documented at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ and is described in a later section of the same page ('below').
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents CodePipeline execution modes.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists in the Pulumi docs and describes update conflicts.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can be applied to the environment a deployment job targets, and this prevents concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines YAML stages support a `lockBehavior` property that is set on the stage referencing the environment with the exclusive lock check.
In Azure Pipelines, `runLatest` is the default value of `lockBehavior`.
Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and an older run waiting behind it is passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is evaluated against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, one at a time (in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior).
`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists as the API docs page for the azuredevops CheckExclusiveLock resource.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `args: --yes` passing the flag to `pulumi up`.
Azure Pipelines deployment jobs with `environment: production` and `strategy: runOnce: deploy:` are the correct syntax for a deployment job targeting an environment.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ (the update conflict troubleshooting page) exists.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing prevents concurrent runs on their own.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as limiting TeamCity builds to one concurrent build.
Limiting the TeamCity build configuration to one simultaneous build prevents the build from reaching the point of hitting a Pulumi update conflict.

In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes Pulumi deployments so they don't run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on environments.
Azure Pipelines stages accept a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section with anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn (serialized).
AWS CodePipeline's pipeline execution mode has a `QUEUED` value.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section with anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions.
In TeamCity, setting **Limit the number of simultaneously running builds** to `1` on the build configuration prevents concurrent builds, thereby serializing Pulumi deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named **Limit the number of simultaneously running builds**.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section with anchor #limit-concurrent-builds, and the TeamCity guide describes this setting.
